content.text:
I booked the Northwind demo for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (booking BK-9901).

- **Attendees:** Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor. The Northwind guest is not on the booking, as you asked.
- **Why Ember:** External guests must be in a ground-floor room under the room-booking policy (SP-2026-5). Ember is on the North building's ground floor and seats 6, so it fits all three. Maple, the only other ground-floor room that fits, had no free hour inside the guest's 10:00–15:00 window.
- **Why 13:30:** This was the only 60-minute slot that fits everyone. It avoids the 12:00–13:00 blackout, Ben's 1:1 at 13:00–13:30, and Ana's roadmap review at 14:30. It also stays inside the guest's window.

I assumed headquarters time is the same as the New York time on Ana's and Ben's calendars (both UTC-5). If headquarters time differs, the guest's window needs rechecking.

content.text:
The Northwind demo is booked for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (R-EMBER), booking ID BK-9901. Attendees are Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor.

Ember was the only room that fit every constraint:
- **Ground floor:** Ember is on floor 0 in the North building, as the policy requires for meetings with external guests.
- **Capacity:** it seats 6, enough for three people.
- **Guest window:** 13:30–14:30 falls inside the Northwind guest's 10:00–15:00 availability.
- **Blackout:** the slot clears the 12:00–13:00 midday blackout.
- **Availability:** Ben's 1:1 ends at 13:30 and Ana is free until her 14:30 meeting, and Ember is open for the whole slot.

The only other ground-floor room that fits three people is Maple, but it is booked from 09:30 to 12:00 and again from 13:00 to 14:30, so no 60-minute slot fit the guest's window.

I used headquarters time as America/New_York, since that is the time zone on Ana's and Ben's calendars. The guest is not on the invite, since they have no calendar here.

content.text:
I booked the Northwind demo for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (booking BK-9901). Attendees are Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor.

Ember is the only room that fits every constraint:
- **External guest:** the policy requires a ground-floor room, and Ember is on floor 0 in North. Maple is also on floor 0, but it is booked until 12:00 and then falls in the midday blackout, so it had no usable slot before the guest's 15:00 cutoff.
- **Capacity:** Ember seats 6, enough for the two employees plus the guest.
- **Availability:** Ember is free from 13:30. Ben's 1:1 ends at 13:30 and Ana is free until her 14:30 meeting.
- **Blackout:** the 13:30–14:30 slot stays clear of the 12:00–13:00 blackout.
- **Guest window:** the meeting sits inside the guest's 10:00–15:00 window.

I took "headquarters time" to be the same as the calendars' time zone (America/New_York), since both employees are on that zone. The guest is not on the invite, as you asked.

content.text:
The Northwind demo is booked for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (booking BK-9901). Attendees are Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor.

Ember is the only slot that works under the policy:
- **Ground floor:** Ember is on floor 0, which the policy requires for meetings with external guests.
- **Capacity:** it seats 6, enough for the three of you.
- **Blackout:** the 12:00–13:00 blackout is avoided.
- **Availability:** Ben is busy 13:00–13:30 and Ana 14:30–16:00, and Ember is free 13:30–14:30.
- **Guest window:** the slot is inside the Northwind guest's 10:00–15:00 window.

Maple is the only other ground-floor room with capacity for three, but it has no free hour that clears the blackout and the guest window.

I assumed "headquarters time" is America/New_York, the time zone on Ana's and Ben's calendars. The guest is not on the booking, since you asked for only the two employees to be attendees.

content.text:
I booked the Northwind demo for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (booking BK-9901). Attendees are Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor.

- **Room:** Ember is on the ground floor, as the policy requires for external guests. It seats 6, so it fits all three people.
- **Blackout:** the slot avoids the 12:00–13:00 midday blackout.
- **Guest window:** 13:30–14:30 falls within the Northwind guest's 10:00–15:00 availability.
- **Calendars:** Ana and Ben are both free for the whole hour.

This was the only option. The other ground-floor room that seats three, Maple, is booked from 13:00 to 14:30, and Ember's earlier slots clash with other bookings or the blackout.

I assumed headquarters time matches the employees' calendar time zone (America/New_York, UTC-5), since the policy doesn't state a headquarters zone. If headquarters is on a different zone, the time will need checking.

The external guest isn't on the booking, since they have no calendar here.

transcript.content: Today is 2026-11-02. The room must seat all three and the booking must follow the room-booking policy. Book only the two employees as attendees; the guest has no calendar here. Meetings start on the hour or half hour.

I booked the Northwind demo for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (booking BK-9901). Attendees are Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor.

- **Room:** Ember is on the ground floor, which the policy requires for meetings with external guests, and it seats 6.
- **Policy:** The slot stays clear of the 12:00–13:00 blackout.
- **Guest window:** 13:30–14:30 falls inside the Northwind guest's 10:00–15:00 availability.

This was the only option that fit. Ember is busy 09:30–11:30 and Maple (the other ground-floor room that seats 3 or more) is busy 09:30–12:00, which rules out the morning. The afternoon has only one usable slot: Ana is busy from 14:30, so a later start would run past the guest's 15:00 cutoff.

I assumed headquarters time matches the New York time on Ana's and Ben's calendars. The tools don't state an HQ offset, so please confirm that. If HQ is on a different clock, the 13:30 start would need to move.

The Northwind guest isn't on the booking because they have no calendar here, so they'll need to be invited separately.

Ember is on the ground floor, which the external-guest rule requires, and it seats 6, so it fits the guest plus both employees. I assumed the booking system's headquarters time matches the New York time on the calendars (both are UTC-5). The guest is not on the booking, since they have no calendar here.

I booked the Northwind demo for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (R-EMBER), booking ID BK-9901.

- **Attendees:** Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor. The Northwind guest is not on the booking, as you asked.
- **Room:** Ember is on the North building's ground floor, so it meets the external-guest rule. It seats 6, which covers the three people.
- **Policy:** The meeting sits outside the 12:00–13:00 blackout window.
- **Guest window:** 13:30–14:30 falls inside the guest's 10:00–15:00 availability.

Only this slot worked. Ana is busy from 14:30, Ben from 13:00 to 13:30, and the other ground-floor rooms that seat three or more were occupied or inside the blackout window at every other time that suits the guest.

I assumed headquarters time matches the New York time shown on the calendars, since both attendees are in that zone.

The "Northwind demo" is booked for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (R-EMBER), booking ID BK-9901.

- **Attendees:** Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor. The Northwind guest is not added because they have no ID in the system.
- **Room:** Ember is on the ground floor of the North building, seats 6, and meets the policy rule that external meetings are on floor 0. It is the only room that fit: the other ground-floor room with enough seats, Maple, has no free slot in the guest's 10:00–15:00 window outside the 12:00–13:00 blackout.
- **Timing:** It avoids Ben's 13:00–13:30 one-to-one and Ana's 14:30 roadmap review, and it stays out of the midday blackout.

I took headquarters time to be the same as the employees' calendar time (UTC−5). If HQ is on a different clock, the time would need checking. The Northwind guest also needs to be told about the 13:30 start.

I booked the Northwind demo for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (booking BK-9901).

- **Attendees:** Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor. The Northwind guest is not on the booking, since they have no calendar here.
- **Room:** Ember is on the ground floor of the North building and seats 6, so it fits all three. External guests must meet on floor 0 under the policy (SP-2026-5).
- **Policy:** The meeting stays clear of the 12:00–13:00 blackout.
- **Guest window:** 13:30–14:30 falls inside the guest's 10:00–15:00 availability.

This was the only option that works. The other ground-floor rooms (Nook, Opal) seat only 2, and Maple was booked or ruled out by Ana's 14:30 commitment. Ember was free from 11:30 to 14:30, and the blackout ruled out the 11:30 start.

I assumed headquarters time matches the New York time zone on Ana's and Ben's calendars (UTC-5). If headquarters is on a different time zone, the time needs checking.

content.text:
I booked the Northwind demo for 2026-11-03 from 13:30 to 14:30 in Ember (booking BK-9901). Attendees are Ana Ruiz and Ben Okafor.

- **Room:** Ember is on the ground floor, which the policy requires for meetings with external guests. It seats 6, so it fits the three of you.
- **Guest window:** The slot falls within the Northwind guest's 10:00–15:00 availability.
- **Policy:** The meeting doesn't touch the 12:00–13:00 midday blackout.
- **Calendars:** Ben's 1:1 ends at 13:30 and Ana's roadmap review starts at 14:30, so both employees are free for the whole slot.

I assumed headquarters time matches the employees' calendar time zone (America/New_York, UTC−5). If HQ is on a different clock, the slot would need to move.

Ember's ground-floor alternative, Maple, couldn't work because its free time starts at 14:30, after the guest's window closes.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 is moved and now includes Eli Novak.

- **Cancelled:** BK-7731, the original 10:00–11:30 slot in Birch.
- **New booking:** BK-9901, "Q4 planning" in **Dune** (floor 1, seats 6, whiteboard), **15:00–16:30** headquarters time, 90 minutes, with Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli.

15:00–16:30 was the only 90-minute slot where all five were free within their working hours. Eli is busy 10:00–13:00, and the other slots were blocked by Ana's 14:00 meeting or Chloe's 16:30 handover. Lark, Cedar and Grove had whiteboards but were already booked at that time.

The original booking was fortnightly, but the new one is a single occurrence. I had no way to set a recurrence, so if the series should continue, it will need to be recreated separately. Ana's fortnightly series may also have been affected by the cancellation, so please check that.

content.text: The new booking is confirmed, so I'll now cancel the original.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has been moved from 10:00–11:30 in Birch to **15:00–16:30 in Dune** (booking BK-9901). It is still 90 minutes and includes all five attendees: Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli.

- **Why this slot:** It was the only 90-minute window in which all five were free within their 09:00–17:00 working hours. Earlier options were blocked by Eli's training and lunch, and by Ana's 14:00 call.
- **Why this room:** Dune seats 6, has a whiteboard, and is free for the slot.
- **Original booking:** BK-7731 is cancelled.

The original booking was a fortnightly recurring series. I cancelled it by its booking ID, so the system may have removed the whole series, not only the 3 November occurrence. Please check whether the future Q4 planning occurrences still exist and re-create them if needed.

I assumed headquarters time matches the New York time shown on everyone's calendars, since the calendar times lined up with the booking times.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has been moved and now includes Eli Novak.

- **New booking:** BK-9901, Dune (North building, floor 1), 15:00–16:30 headquarters time (90 minutes).
- **Attendees:** Ana Ruiz, Ben Okafor, Chloe Marsh, Dev Patel and Eli Novak.
- **Room:** Dune has a whiteboard and seats 6.
- **Cancelled:** the original booking, BK-7731 (Birch, 10:00–11:30).

Everyone is free for the full slot. The 15:00–16:30 window was the only 90-minute slot inside everyone's working hours that worked for all five. Ana has a meeting at 14:00, and Eli is in training from 10:00 to 12:00.

I took headquarters time to be the same as the attendees' calendars (America/New_York, UTC−5), since the system didn't state an HQ offset explicitly. The original booking was part of a fortnightly series, and I only cancelled this one booking ID, so the series may need checking.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 is moved and now includes Eli Novak.

- **Cancelled:** the original booking BK-7731 (Birch, 10:00–11:30).
- **New booking:** BK-9901, "Q4 planning", in Dune (floor 1, North building) from 15:00 to 16:30, which is 90 minutes. The five attendees are Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli.

Dune has a whiteboard and seats six. All five are free and inside their 09:00–17:00 working hours. Everyone is on New York time (UTC−5), which matches the headquarters times I used.

15:00–16:30 was the only 90-minute slot that worked for all five. Morning and early-afternoon options were blocked by Eli's training (10:00–12:00) or Ana's 14:00 meeting. Dune is the only room with a whiteboard and enough seats that was free then.

The original meeting was a fortnightly recurring series. The new booking is a single meeting, and I had no way to set recurrence, so the series no longer exists. If you want it to repeat, it will need to be set up again.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 is moved to **15:00–16:30 in Dune (R-DUNE)**, with all five attendees: Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli.

- **Cancelled:** the original booking BK-7731 (Birch, 10:00–11:30).

Why this slot: Eli is in training 10:00–12:00, and Ana has a meeting 14:00–15:00. That leaves 15:00–16:30 as the only 90-minute window on the hour or half hour when everyone is free. Chloe's handover starts at 16:30, so the meeting ends just as it begins. Dune has a whiteboard and seats six. It was the only room with a whiteboard and enough seats that was free then.

The Q4 planning meeting has been moved to **Tuesday 2026-11-03, 15:00–16:30 (headquarters time) in Dune**, with all five attendees: Ana Ruiz, Ben Okafor, Chloe Marsh, Dev Patel and Eli Novak. The new booking is BK-9901.

- **Room:** Dune seats 6, has a whiteboard, and is free at that time.

The original meeting was fortnightly, but the new booking is a single occurrence (recurrence: none). If you want it to repeat fortnightly, that will need to be set up separately, as the booking tool has no recurrence option.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has been moved and now includes Eli Novak.

- **Cancelled:** the original booking, BK-7731 (Birch, 10:00–11:30, four attendees).
- **New booking:** BK-9901, "Q4 planning" in **Dune** (ground floor, North building, 6 seats, whiteboard), **15:00–16:30** on 2026-11-03. Attendees are Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli.

I picked this slot because it was the only 90-minute window in the day where all five are free within working hours. Dune was the only room with a whiteboard, enough seats and no clash in that window. I treated headquarters time as the same as the attendees' calendar time (America/New_York, UTC-5), since everyone's calendar is in that zone.

The original meeting was fortnightly, but the new booking is a single one-off meeting. If the series should continue, it will need to be set up again as recurring.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has been moved to 15:00–16:30 (headquarters time) in Dune (R-DUNE, floor 1, whiteboard, capacity 6). The new booking is BK-9901, and all five attendees are included: Ana Ruiz, Ben Okafor, Chloe Marsh, Dev Patel and Eli Novak.

- **Cancelled:** the original booking BK-7731 (10:00–11:30 in Birch).
- **Why 15:00–16:30:** it is the only 90-minute slot on the hour or half hour that is inside everyone's working hours and free for all five. Eli is busy until 13:00, and Ana is busy 14:00–15:00.

The original booking was a fortnightly recurring series, but the new one is a single meeting. If the series should continue, the recurrence will need to be set up again. I cancelled only BK-7731 and did not check whether it affected other dates in the series.

Dune has a whiteboard and seats 6. Everyone is free for the full slot within their working hours. I chose 15:00 because it was the only 90-minute window where all five are free and a suitable room is open. Lark, the other option, was booked for a workshop from 14:30.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has been moved and now includes Eli Novak.

- **Cancelled:** the original booking BK-7731 (Birch, 10:00–11:30).

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has been moved and now includes Eli Novak.

- **Cancelled:** BK-7731 (previously 10:00–11:30 in Birch, fortnightly).
- **New booking:** BK-9901, "Q4 planning", 15:00–16:30 in Dune (floor 1, North building). Dune has a whiteboard and seats 6.
- **Attendees:** Ana Ruiz, Ben Okafor, Chloe Marsh, Dev Patel and Eli Novak. All five are free for the full slot within their 09:00–17:00 working hours.

Two things to check:
- **Recurrence:** The original meeting was fortnightly, but the new booking is a single occurrence. I didn't have a way to set a recurrence, so future Q4 planning sessions will need to be rescheduled or re-created separately.
- **Time zone:** Everyone's calendar is on New York time (UTC-5), which I took to be headquarters time, so 15:00 is HQ time.

I chose 15:00 because it was the only 90-minute window that fit everyone. Cedar and Lark were the other rooms with whiteboards that could seat five, but both were already booked then.

- **Cancelled:** the original BK-7731 (10:00–11:30 in Birch).
- **Why 15:00–16:30:** it was the only 90-minute window in everyone's working hours (09:00–17:00, all on the same time zone as headquarters). Eli is in training 10:00–12:00, and the others have lunch 12:00–13:00 and other commitments.
- **Why Dune:** it has a whiteboard and seats six. Lark (5 seats) was taken by the Roadmap workshop, Cedar had a conflict at 15:30, and Grove was booked all day.

The original booking was part of a fortnightly series, and I cancelled the whole booking. Cancelling it may have ended the recurring series, and BK-9901 is a one-off. If the series should continue, the recurrence will need to be set up again.

content.text: The new booking is confirmed, so I'll now cancel the original.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 is moved to 15:00–16:30 (headquarters time) in Dune (R-DUNE, floor 1, whiteboard, seats 6). The new booking is BK-9901, and it includes all five people: Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli.

The original 10:00–11:30 booking (BK-7731) is cancelled. It was a fortnightly series, and the cancellation may have removed its future occurrences too. Check that against what you intended.

I chose 15:00 because it is the only 90-minute slot inside everyone's working hours (09:00–17:00) where all five are free. Eli's 10:00–12:00 training and the 12:00–13:00 lunch blocks ruled out the morning. Ana's 14:00 meeting and Chloe's 16:30 handover ruled out the other afternoon slots. Dune was the only room with a whiteboard and enough seats that was free then. The Cedar and Lark rooms had conflicts.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has moved from 10:00–11:30 to **15:00–16:30 in Dune (R-DUNE)**, with all five attendees: Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli. The new booking is BK-9901, and the original BK-7731 is cancelled.

- **Why this slot:** It is the only 90-minute window on the hour or half hour when all five are free within working hours. Eli is busy 10:00–13:00, and Ana has a meeting at 14:00–15:00.

- **Cancelled:** BK-7731, the original 10:00–11:30 slot in Birch.
- **New booking:** BK-9901, "Q4 planning", 15:00–16:30 (90 minutes) in Dune, with Ana Ruiz, Ben Okafor, Chloe Marsh, Dev Patel and Eli Novak.

Why this slot: 15:00–16:30 was the only time all five were free within 09:00–17:00. Dune has a whiteboard, seats six, and was free then. Birch was too small, and Cedar, Grove and Lark were already booked during that window.

Please check one thing: the original meeting was a fortnightly series, but the new booking is a single meeting with no recurrence. I had no tool to set up a recurring booking, so the series will need to be recreated if you want it to repeat.

The Q4 planning meeting on 2026-11-03 has been moved to **15:00–16:30 HQ time in Dune (R-DUNE)**, with Eli Novak added to the original four attendees.

- **Cancelled:** BK-7731, the original 10:00–11:30 booking in Birch.
- **New booking:** BK-9901, Q4 planning, 15:00–16:30, Dune, attendees Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dev and Eli.

Eli's calendar blocks 10:00–13:00, so 15:00–16:30 was the only 90-minute slot on the hour or half hour when all five were free within working hours. Dune has a whiteboard and seats six. The other whiteboard rooms with enough seats were already booked at that time.

Two things differ from the original booking, and you may want to check them:
- **Recurrence:** BK-7731 was fortnightly, but the new booking is a single meeting. I did not find a way to set a recurrence, so the series will need to be re-created if it should continue.
- **Catering:** The original had a water-only catering order, which did not carry over. Dune does offer catering if it's still needed.

- **T-2103** (Report export is timing out): Pro plan, high blast radius gives high. The customer is flagged as an attrition risk, so it was raised one level to **urgent**.
- **T-2101** (Dashboard widgets misaligned): Enterprise plan, medium blast radius gives **high**. No churn flag and not a security incident.
- **T-2102** (Password reset email looks odd): Category is security_incident, so it is always **urgent** regardless of plan or impact.

All other open tickets already had a priority, so I left them alone.

grade_detail: all tickets in the expected final state

content.text:
Three open tickets have no urgency/priority set: T-2103, T-2101 and T-2102. I'll apply the matrix and override rules to each.

- **T-2103** (pro plan, high blast radius → high; churn-flagged, so raised one level) → **urgent**
- **T-2101** (enterprise plan, medium blast radius → high; no override) → **high**
- **T-2102** (security_incident category → always urgent) → **urgent**

I set priorities on the three open tickets that had none. The other 12 open tickets already had a priority and I left them alone.

- **T-2103** (Report export is timing out): **urgent**. The Pro plan with high blast radius gives high, and the customer is flagged as a churn risk, so it was raised one level.
- **T-2101** (Dashboard widgets misaligned): **high**. The Enterprise plan with medium blast radius gives high, with no override.
- **T-2102** (Password reset email looks odd): **urgent**. It is a security incident, which is always urgent under the rules.

The list and ticket records show this as an "urgency" field, and I treated it as the priority. The tool results confirmed all three updates.

I closed two open tickets as duplicates under policy DP-2026-1. Both match a resolved ticket on product area and error code.

- **T-4103** ("Staff cannot sign in through Okta", auth, SSO-114) closed as a duplicate of **T-4090** ("SAML login loop").
- **T-4101** ("Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup", webhooks, WH-429) closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** ("Webhook retries stop after 3 attempts").

I left **T-4104** open. It shares error code SSO-114 with T-4090, but it is in the mobile_app product area, not auth, so the policy doesn't treat it as a duplicate.

No other open ticket matched a resolved ticket on both product area and error code, so I didn't change them.

I closed two open tickets as duplicates under policy DP-2026-1. Both match a resolved ticket on the same product area and error code.

I left **T-4104** open. It has the same error code as T-4090 (SSO-114), but it is in the mobile_app product area rather than auth, so the policy does not treat it as a duplicate.

The other open tickets have error codes that don't match any resolved ticket, so I did not change them.

I closed two open tickets as duplicates. I checked each open ticket against the two resolved tickets (T-4090 and T-4100) under duplicate policy DP-2026-1, which requires the same product area and the same error code.

**Closed as duplicates:**
- **T-4103** (Staff cannot sign in through Okta, SSO-114, auth) → duplicate of **T-4090** (SAML login loop, SSO-114, auth)
- **T-4101** (Callbacks stop arriving, WH-429, webhooks) → duplicate of **T-4100** (Webhook retries stop after 3 attempts, WH-429, webhooks)

**Left open:**
- **T-4104** (Mobile app shows SSO-114). It has the same error code as T-4090, but its product area is mobile_app, not auth, so it does not meet the policy.
- **T-4102** (WH-503). No resolved ticket has this error code.
- The other open tickets have error codes that match no resolved ticket.

content.text:
I closed two open tickets as duplicates of resolved tickets. I left the other open tickets alone.

- **T-4101** (callbacks stop after a hiccup, WH-429) closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** (webhook retries, WH-429). Both are in the webhooks component area with the same error code.
- **T-4103** (staff cannot sign in through Okta, SSO-114) closed as a duplicate of **T-4090** (SAML login loop, SSO-114). Both are in the auth component area with the same error code.

I did not close **T-4104** (mobile app shows SSO-114 after update). It has the same error code as T-4090, but its component area is mobile_app, not auth, so it does not meet the policy's same-product-area requirement. It needs a human decision.

I also did not close **T-4102** (webhook retries stop after 3 attempts, WH-503). No resolved ticket has that error code. The remaining open tickets have error codes that match no resolved ticket.

I used the ticket's component area as the "product area" from the policy. For T-4101 the desk differs from T-4100 (intake vs. payments). If Support Operations reads "product area" as the desk, that closure should be reviewed.

I left the other open tickets alone. T-4104 also shows SSO-114, but it is in the mobile_app area rather than auth, so it does not qualify. The rest of the open tickets have no matching resolved ticket.

content.text:
I closed two open tickets as duplicates under policy DP-2026-1. Both are duplicates on product area and error code.

- **T-4103** ("Staff cannot sign in through Okta") closed as a duplicate of **T-4090** (SSO-114, auth).
- **T-4101** ("Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup") closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** (WH-429, webhooks).

I left the other open tickets alone. **T-4104** shares error code SSO-114 with T-4090 but is in the mobile_app area rather than auth, so it does not meet the policy. The rest have no matching resolved ticket.

Both closed tickets show a different desk from their resolved match (intake versus identity or payments). I matched on component area because the policy says product area, not queue. If you consider desk the product area, T-4101 and T-4103 would not qualify.

- **T-4101** ("Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup", WH-429, webhooks) closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** ("Webhook retries stop after 3 attempts").

I left the other open tickets alone:
- **T-4104** shares error code SSO-114 with T-4090, but its product area is mobile_app, not auth, so it doesn't meet the policy.
- **T-4102** has a title similar to T-4100, but its error code is WH-503, not WH-429.
- The remaining open tickets have error codes that don't match any resolved ticket.

content.text:
I closed two open tickets as duplicates. The other eleven open tickets were left alone.

**Closed as duplicates (per policy DP-2026-1, same product area and error code as a resolved ticket):**
- **T-4103** (Staff cannot sign in through Okta, SSO-114, auth) → duplicate of **T-4090** (SAML login loop, SSO-114, auth).
- **T-4101** (Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup, WH-429, webhooks) → duplicate of **T-4100** (Webhook retries stop after 3 attempts, WH-429, webhooks).

**Not closed:**
- **T-4104** shares error code SSO-114 with T-4090, but its product area is mobile_app, not auth, so the policy does not treat it as a duplicate.
- The remaining open tickets (T-4102, T-4105, T-4106, T-4107, T-4108, T-4109, T-4110, T-4111, T-4112, T-4113) have no resolved ticket with a matching product area and error code.

content.text:
I closed two open tickets as duplicates under policy DP-2026-1, which requires a matching product area and error code with a resolved ticket:

- **T-4103** (Staff cannot sign in through Okta): closed as a duplicate of **T-4090** (SAML login loop). Both are in the auth area with error SSO-114.
- **T-4101** (Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup): closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** (Webhook retries stop after 3 attempts). Both are in the webhooks area with error WH-429.

I left these open because they don't meet the policy:
- **T-4104** (mobile app shows SSO-114): same error code as T-4090, but it is in mobile_app rather than auth.
- **T-4102** (webhook retries stop after 3 attempts): similar wording to T-4100, but its error code is WH-503, not WH-429.

I did not touch any other open tickets.

content.text:
I closed 2 open tickets as duplicates, each pointing to the resolved ticket it duplicates:

- **T-4103** (Staff cannot sign in through Okta) → duplicate of **T-4090** (SAML login loop). Both are in the auth product area with error code SSO-114.
- **T-4101** (Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup) → duplicate of **T-4100** (Webhook retries stop after 3 attempts). Both are in the webhooks product area with error code WH-429.

I left these open because they don't meet the policy's test (same product area and same error code as a resolved ticket):

- **T-4104** has the same SSO-114 code as T-4090, but it is in the mobile_app area rather than auth.
- **T-4102** has a similar subject to T-4100, but its error code is WH-503, not WH-429.
- The remaining open tickets have no resolved ticket with a matching error code.

I closed two open tickets as duplicates under policy DP-2026-1, which requires the same product area and the same error code as a resolved ticket.

- **T-4103** ("Staff cannot sign in through Okta") closed as a duplicate of **T-4090**. Both are in the auth product area with error code SSO-114.

I left the other open tickets alone:
- **T-4104** has the same error code as T-4090 (SSO-114), but it is in the mobile_app product area, not auth, so it does not qualify.
- **T-4102** (WH-503), **T-4105**, **T-4106**, **T-4107**, **T-4108**, **T-4109**, **T-4110**, **T-4111**, **T-4112** and **T-4113** have no matching resolved ticket with the same product area and error code.

I closed two open tickets as duplicates. Both match a resolved ticket on product area and error code, as duplicate policy DP-2026-1 requires.

- **T-4103** ("Staff cannot sign in through Okta") is closed as a duplicate of **T-4090** (auth, SSO-114).
- **T-4101** ("Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup") is closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** (webhooks, WH-429).

I left **T-4104** open. It has the same error code as T-4090 (SSO-114), but it is in the mobile_app product area, not auth, so the policy does not treat it as a duplicate.

The other open tickets have error codes that match no resolved ticket, so I did not touch them.

content.text:
I closed two open tickets as duplicates. Both matched a resolved ticket on product area and error code, as duplicate policy DP-2026-1 requires.

- **T-4103** ("Staff cannot sign in through Okta") closed as a duplicate of **T-4090** (auth, SSO-114).
- **T-4101** ("Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup") closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** (webhooks, WH-429).

I left the other 11 open tickets alone. None of them matched a resolved ticket on both product area and error code. The closest near-misses were:
- **T-4104** shares error code SSO-114 with T-4090, but it is in mobile_app, not auth.
- **T-4102** shares a subject with T-4100, but its error code is WH-503, not WH-429.

- **T-4101** (Callbacks stop arriving after a hiccup) closed as a duplicate of **T-4100** (Webhook retries stop after 3 attempts). Both are webhooks / WH-429.

- **T-4104** has the same error code as T-4090 (SSO-114), but it is in the mobile_app area, not auth, so it does not meet the policy.

- **Ticket with a reply:** T-5117 has a first reply, so it was not checked against the clock.

I escalated **T-5101** ("Payment webhooks delayed") to the on-call duty manager. Its status is now escalated.

It is the only open ticket in breach. It is an enterprise customer's urgent ticket with a 1-hour first-response target. It was created at 08:30 and had no first response at 12:00, so it had been waiting 3.5 hours.

I checked the other unanswered tickets that could have breached under some plan. None breach for their actual plan:
- **T-5104** (pro, high, 4h target): 3h elapsed.

- **T-5102** (free, normal, 72h target): about 51h elapsed.
- **T-5108** (free, urgent, 8h target): 1.5h elapsed.

No other ticket was escalated.

content.text:
I escalated T-5101 ("Payment webhooks delayed") to the on-call duty manager. It is the only open ticket that breaches its first-response SLA.

- **Breach:** Enterprise plan, urgent priority, 1-hour target. Created 08:30 with no first response, so 3.5 hours have elapsed at 12:00.
- **Other open tickets checked:** No other open ticket with no first response is past its target for its plan. The closest were T-5104 (pro, high, 3h against a 4h target) and T-5106 (pro, high, 2.5h against a 4h target). T-5102 (free, normal, 51h against 72h) and T-5107 (pro, normal, 11h against 24h) are also within target.
- **Assumption:** T-5105 has no plan in the list data, so I didn't fetch its record. It would only breach if it were enterprise with a target under its 6-hour age, and the enterprise normal target is 8 hours, so it can't breach.

The ticket now shows as escalated, updated at 12:00.

content.text:
I escalated **T-5101** ("Payment webhooks delayed") to the on-call duty manager. It is the only open ticket that has breached its first-response SLA.

- **Why it breaches:** It is urgent priority on an enterprise plan (Lumen Energy). The target is 1 hour, and it was created at 08:30 with no first response, so the clock was at 3.5 hours at 12:00.
- **Why the others don't:** I checked every open ticket with no first response against its plan and priority. The closest candidates were all within target:
  - T-5104 (pro, high): 3h elapsed against a 4h target.
  - T-5106 (pro, high): 2.5h against 4h.
  - T-5108 (free, urgent): 1.5h against 8h.
  - T-5107 (pro, normal): 11h against 24h.
  - T-5102 (free, normal): 50h against 72h.
  - The remaining tickets are either too recent to breach under any plan or are low priority with targets longer than their age.

No other tickets were escalated.

- **Checked and not breached:** I checked every open ticket with no first response, using each customer's plan and priority. Each is within its target. The closest was T-5106 (pro, high, 4h target, 2.5h elapsed).
- **Not checked:** Open tickets that already have a first response are outside the breach test, so I did not evaluate them.

No other ticket was escalated.

- **T-6102** (Sync fails again): the patch worked briefly, but the sync is failing again.
- **T-6104** (Calendar feed not updating): the customer explicitly asked not to close until it works.
- **T-6106** (Shared folder permissions reset): still broken, and the customer is asking for an update.

I closed four tickets as resolved. The other two open tickets stay open.

**Closed (customer asked for closure because the problem is fixed):**
- **T-6103** (Sync outage on EU region): "Confirmed working on our side now."
- **T-6105** (Cannot reach API from office): the cause was their firewall, and it's sorted on their end.
- **T-6101** (Sync fails for shared folders): "Your patch fixed it for us." It was linked to T-6103, so I closed T-6103 first.

**Left open:**
- **T-6102** (Sync fails again): the patch worked yesterday, but the sync is failing again, so the problem isn't fixed.
- **T-6104** (Calendar feed not updating): the customer asked not to close it until it works.
- **T-6106** (Shared folder permissions reset): still broken, and the customer is asking for an update.

I closed 4 of the 6 open tickets as resolved. The other 2 stay open.

**Closed (customer asked for closure and the problem is fixed):**
- **T-6103** (Sync outage on EU region): "Confirmed working on our side now."
- **T-6105** (Cannot reach API from office): the cause was the customer's firewall, and it is sorted on their end.
- **T-6101** (Sync fails for shared folders): "Your patch fixed it for us." I closed this after T-6103 because it was blocked by T-6103, and the system would not close it before its parent was closed.

**Left open:**
- **T-6102** (Sync fails again): the patch worked briefly, but the sync is failing again, so it is not fixed.
- **T-6104** (Calendar feed not updating): the customer explicitly asked not to close it until it works.
- **T-6106** (Shared folder permissions reset): still broken, and the customer is asking for an update.
